## Admin Page Implementation Analysis

Based on my thorough exploration of the Safecast New Map codebase, here's the complete breakdown of the admin page structure and implementation:

### 1. **Admin Pages Overview**

The project has **three main admin pages** currently implemented:

- **User Administration**: `/admin/users` - Manage users (CRUD operations)
- **Uploads Administration**: `/admin/uploads` - View and manage file uploads
- **Tracks Administration**: `/admin/tracks` - View and manage GPS tracks

### 2. **HTML Templates**

#### Main Admin User Page
- **Location**: `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/unified-server/public_html/admin-users.html`
- **Size**: ~847 lines
- **Structure**:
  - Uses embedded CSS with CSS custom properties (variables) for theming
  - Supports light/dark mode via media queries and data-theme attributes
  - Responsive design with flexbox layout
  - Self-contained HTML with embedded JavaScript

**Key Sections**:
- Navigation bar with action buttons (Add User, Delete Selected, Back to Map)
- Summary section with pagination controls and search
- Data table with sortable columns and filter inputs
- Pagination controls (top and bottom)
- Modal dialog for Add/Edit user operations

#### Admin Uploads & Tracks Pages
- **Generated dynamically** in Go handlers (not separate HTML files)
- Locations: Built inline in `main.go` at lines 5039+ and 6349+
- Generated with embedded HTML strings in Go code

### 3. **Go Handler Structure**

#### Route Registration (`pkg/httpapi/register.go`)
```
/api/admin/users         → AdminListUsersHandler (GET)
/api/admin/users/create  → AdminCreateUserHandler (POST)
/api/admin/users/{id}    → AdminUpdateUserHandler (PUT/PATCH)
/api/admin/users/{id}    → AdminDeleteUserHandler (DELETE)
/api/admin/users/{id}/reset-password    → AdminResetUserPasswordHandler (POST)
/api/admin/users/{id}/regenerate-api-key → AdminRegenerateAPIKeyHandler (POST)
```

#### Page Serving Routes (`cmd/unified-server/main.go`)
```
/admin/users  → Serves HTML template from embedded content
/admin/uploads → Calls adminUploadsHandler (generates HTML with embedded JS)
```

#### Handler Functions Location
- **Admin User Handlers**: `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/pkg/auth/admin_handlers.go` (lines 1-430)
- **Admin Uploads Handler**: `cmd/unified-server/main.go` (line 4970)
- **Admin Tracks Handler**: `cmd/unified-server/main.go` (line 6186)

### 4. **Admin Authentication Pattern**

Two-layer authentication approach:

**Layer 1: Middleware** (`pkg/auth/middleware.go`)
- `OptionalAuth()` - Attempts to authenticate via session, doesn't fail if not authenticated
- `RequireAuth()` - Requires session authentication
- Both look for user context via `auth.GetUserFromContext()`

**Layer 2: Admin Access Check** (in `register.go` and `main.go`)
- Function: `checkAdminAccess()` (pkg/httpapi/register.go, line 136-145)
- Also: `checkAdminAuth()` (cmd/unified-server/main.go, line 4944)

**Authentication Priority**:
1. **Session-based**: Check if user is logged in via session AND has `is_admin=true`
2. **Fallback**: Check for URL parameter `?password=xxx` matching `adminPassword` flag

**Code Pattern**:
```go
func checkAdminAccess(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, adminPassword string) bool {
    if user, ok := auth.GetUserFromContext(r.Context()); ok && user.IsAdmin {
        return true
    }
    if adminPassword != "" && r.URL.Query().Get("password") == adminPassword {
        return true
    }
    http.Error(w, "Unauthorized - Please login as admin or provide password", http.StatusUnauthorized)
    return false
}
```

### 5. **Navigation/Layout Pattern**

All admin pages use a consistent navigation pattern:

**Top Navigation Bar** (`.nav` class):
- `.nav-left` - Contains navigation links and action buttons
- Navigation links to other admin pages (cross-linking)
- Action buttons (Add, Delete, Backfill, etc.)
- `.back-to-map-btn` - Blue button to return to main map

**Visual Hierarchy**:
```
H1 Title
├── Navigation Bar (.nav)
├── Summary/Status Section
├── Main Content (Table)
└── Pagination Controls
```

**Example Navigation**:
- Uploads page: Links to "All Tracks" and "Tracked Uploads"
- Tracks page: Links to "All Tracks" and "Tracked Uploads"

### 6. **Styling System**

All admin pages use **CSS custom properties** for consistent theming:

**Light Mode Variables**:
```css
--bg-primary: #f5f5f5
--bg-card: white
--text-primary: #333
--text-secondary: #666
--border-color: #ddd
--link-color: #0066cc
--th-bg: #424242
```

**Dark Mode Variables** (via `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` or `[data-theme='dark']`):
```css
--bg-primary: #1a1a1a
--bg-card: #2b2b2b
--text-primary: #eee
--text-secondary: #aaa
--border-color: #444
--link-color: #90caf9
--th-bg: #616161
```

**Reusable Component Classes**:
- `.badge` / `.badge-active` / `.badge-inactive` - Status indicators
- `.btn-primary` / `.btn-secondary` / `.btn-danger` - Button styles
- `.modal` / `.modal-content` / `.modal-header` - Dialog patterns
- `.pagination-btn` - Pagination styling
- `.sortable` - Sortable column headers

### 7. **UI Patterns Already in Use**

**Sortable Tables** (admin-users.html, lines 84-88):
```javascript
.sortable { cursor: pointer; user-select: none; position: relative; padding-right: 20px; }
.sortable::after { content: '⇅'; position: absolute; right: 8px; opacity: 0.5; }
.sortable.asc::after { content: '▲'; opacity: 1; }
.sortable.desc::after { content: '▼'; opacity: 1; }
```

**Client-Side Filtering** (lines 608-631):
```javascript
function filterTable() {
    // Filters applied per column via input fields
}
```

**Modal Dialogs** (lines 112-309):
```html
.modal { display: none; position: fixed; z-index: 1000; ... }
<!-- Modal content structure -->
```

**Pagination Controls** (lines 138-150):
- First/Prev/Next/Last buttons
- Page number buttons with ellipsis
- Page size selector (25, 50, 100, 200 items)

**Search/Filter Bar** (lines 180-186):
```html
<input type="text" id="searchInput" placeholder="Search email, username, ID...">
<button class="search-btn" onclick="doSearch()">Search</button>
```

**No Tabbed UI Currently**: 
- No native tab components found in existing admin pages
- All pages use full-page layout with cross-page navigation instead

### 8. **Data Flow for Admin Users**

**Frontend** (admin-users.html):
1. User navigates to `/admin/users` with optional `?password=xxx`
2. HTML page loads and checks authentication on DOMContentLoaded
3. Calls `/api/admin/users?limit=50&offset=0` to fetch user list
4. Displays paginated table with search/filter
5. User interactions (add, edit, delete) call respective API endpoints

**Backend** (pkg/auth/admin_handlers.go):
1. Request arrives at authenticated route
2. `checkAdminAccess()` verifies session or password
3. Handler function processes request:
   - `AdminListUsersHandler()` - Returns JSON list with pagination
   - `AdminCreateUserHandler()` - Creates user, sends welcome email if configured
   - `AdminUpdateUserHandler()` - Updates fields, handles optional password
   - `AdminDeleteUserHandler()` - Soft or hard delete
   - `AdminResetUserPasswordHandler()` - Creates reset token, sends email

### 9. **Key Technical Details**

**Authentication Context** (`pkg/auth/middleware.go`):
- User stored in request context via `WithAuthContext()`
- Retrieved with `GetUserFromContext()`
- User model includes: `ID`, `Email`, `Username`, `IsAdmin`, `IsActive`, `EmailVerified`, `APIKey`, etc.

**Database Operations** (`pkg/auth/database.go`):
- `GetUsersPaginated()` - Fetch paginated list
- `CountUsers()` - Get total count for pagination
- `CreateUser()` - Insert new user with hashed password
- `UpdateUser()` - Update user record
- `DeleteUser()` - Remove user from database

**Password Reset Flow**:
1. Admin triggers reset via "Reset Password" button
2. Backend generates token, stores in `password_reset_tokens` table
3. Email sent with reset link (7-day expiry for admin-initiated, 1-hour default)
4. User clicks link to `/reset-password?token=xxx`
5. User sets new password, token marked as used

### 10. **File Locations Summary**

| Component | Location |
|-----------|----------|
| Admin Users HTML | `cmd/unified-server/public_html/admin-users.html` |
| Admin Handlers (Users) | `pkg/auth/admin_handlers.go` |
| Route Registration | `pkg/httpapi/register.go` |
| Page Serving | `cmd/unified-server/main.go` (lines 8828-8872) |
| Uploads Handler | `cmd/unified-server/main.go` (lines 4970-5755) |
| Tracks Handler | `cmd/unified-server/main.go` (lines 6186-6810) |
| Middleware | `pkg/auth/middleware.go` |
| Auth Context | `pkg/auth/auth.go` |
| User Models | `pkg/auth/models.go` |

This comprehensive structure provides a solid foundation for extending admin functionality. The dual authentication pattern (session + password) is flexible, and the CSS theming system makes styling consistent and maintainable across all admin pages.

## Comprehensive Analysis: MCP Server Analytics and DuckLake Data Structures

I've completed a thorough exploration of the MCP server analytics and DuckLake implementation. Here's the complete picture:

### 1. DuckLake Tables: Schemas and DDL

All three analytics tables are created identically in both MCP server and unified server during initialization:

#### **mcp_query_log** (Tool execution usage statistics)
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mcp_query_log (
    tool_name VARCHAR,
    timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    duration_ms BIGINT,
    result_count INTEGER,
    client VARCHAR,
    user_id VARCHAR,
    user_email VARCHAR
)
```

**Source files:**
- `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/mcp-server/duckdb_client.go` (lines 85-92)
- `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/unified-server/duckdb_analytics.go` (lines 112-120)

#### **mcp_ai_query_log** (AI tool execution and query logs)
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mcp_ai_query_log (
    user_id VARCHAR,
    user_email VARCHAR,
    session_id VARCHAR,
    timestamp TIMESTAMP,
    tool_name VARCHAR,
    generated_query VARCHAR,
    duration_ms BIGINT,
    commit_hash VARCHAR,
    error VARCHAR
)
```

**Source files:**
- `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/mcp-server/duckdb_client.go` (lines 93-103)
- `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/unified-server/duckdb_analytics.go` (lines 121-131)

#### **chat_questions** (Web-chat and map widget questions with full metadata)
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chat_questions (
    id BIGINT,
    timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    question VARCHAR,
    source VARCHAR,
    ip_address VARCHAR,
    user_agent VARCHAR,
    is_mobile BOOLEAN,
    os VARCHAR,
    browser VARCHAR,
    country VARCHAR,
    accept_language VARCHAR,
    referer VARCHAR,
    session_id VARCHAR,
    history_length INTEGER,
    model VARCHAR,
    cloudfront BOOLEAN,
    client_timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ,
    answer VARCHAR
)
```

**Source files:**
- `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/mcp-server/duckdb_client.go` (lines 104-123)
- `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/unified-server/duckdb_analytics.go` (lines 132-151)

---

### 2. How Analytics Data is Written

#### **MCP Query Log (tool usage)**

**MCP Server:**
- Location: `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/mcp-server/duckdb_client.go` (lines 136-159)
- Function: `LogQueryAsync(toolName string, params map[string]any, resultCount int, duration time.Duration, clientInfo string)`
- Called from: `instrument()` wrapper in `main.go` (line 74)
- Inserts asynchronously via goroutine
- Parameters JSON-encoded and stored in params field

**Unified Server:**
- Location: `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/unified-server/mcp_db_helpers.go` (lines 67-94)
- Function: `LogQueryAsync(name string, args map[string]any, resultCount int, duration time.Duration, client string)`
- Called from: `instrumentMCP()` wrapper in `mcp_register.go` (line 510)
- Extracts user_id and user_email from tool arguments
- Async insertion with silent error handling

#### **AI Query Log (tool execution with query details)**

**MCP Server:**
- Location: `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/mcp-server/ai_logging.go` (lines 34-82, 85-130)
- Function: `logAISessionWithUser(toolName, query, duration, err, userID, userEmail)`
- Async logging to DuckDB table `mcp_ai_query_log`
- Sanitizes query (collapses whitespace, removes string literals)
- Truncates queries to 1000 chars
- Generates RFC4122 v4 UUIDs for session IDs
- Includes git commit hash (cached on first call)

**Unified Server:**
- Location: `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/unified-server/ai_logging.go` (identical code)
- Called from: `instrumentMCP()` in `mcp_register.go` (lines 512-519)

**Key data collection:**
- `user_id`, `user_email`: Extracted from MCP request arguments
- `session_id`: Generated random UUID v4
- `timestamp`: RFC3339 format (UTC)
- `generated_query`: Sanitized SQL/query string
- `duration_ms`: Milliseconds
- `commit_hash`: Git HEAD revision
- `error`: Error message (if any)

#### **Chat Questions (web-chat analytics)**

**Location:** `/home/rob/Documents/Safecast/safecast-new-map/cmd/unified-server/chat_logging.go` (lines 14-78)

**Function:** `logChatQuestion(r *http.Request, question, source, model, sessionID string, historyLen int, clientTimestamp string) int64`
- Called from: `handleWebChat()` in `mcp_register.go` (line 209)
- Inserts question record and returns auto-generated ID
- Uses `time.Now().UnixNano()` for unique ID (DuckLake has no RETURNING or sequences)
- Extracts metadata from HTTP request headers:
  - IP address (respects X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP proxies)
  - User-Agent header (parses Mobile/Desktop, OS, Browser)
  - CloudFront headers detection
  - CloudFront-Viewer-Country
  - Accept-Language
  - Referer
- Caps question at 5000 chars

**Answer logging:** `logChatAnswer(rowID int64, answer string)`
- Updates the same row asynchronously with AI response
- Async to avoid blocking chat response
- Caps answer at 50,000 chars

---

### 3. How Analytics Data is Currently Queried/Read

# Plan: Admin MCP Analytics Page with Tabbed Navigation ## Context The MCP server and web-chat collect analytics into 3 DuckLake tables (`chat_questions`, `mcp_query_log`, `mcp_ai_query_log`) but there's no admin UI to browse this data. The user wants a new admin page to view/search/export MCP analytics, and to reorganize all admin pages under a tabbed navigation system. ## Approach ### 1. Add tabbed navigation to all admin pages - Create a shared tab bar component (HTML/CSS snippet) used across all admin pages - Tabs: **Users** | **Uploads** | **Tracks** | **MCP Analytics** | ~~Realtime~~ (greyed out, future) - Active tab highlighted based on current page - Each tab links to its respective `/admin/*` route - Update existing pages (admin-users.html, uploads handler, tracks handler) to include the tab bar ### 2. Create new MCP Analytics admin page **New file:** `cmd/unified-server/public_html/admin-mcp.html` Self-contained HTML page (same pattern as admin-users.html) with: **Sub-tabs** within the MCP page for the 3 tables: - **Chat Questions** — `chat_questions` table (default view) - **Tool Usage** — `mcp_query_log` table - **AI Query Log** — `mcp_ai_query_log` table **Features per sub-tab:** - Sortable data table showing ALL fields from each table - Column filter inputs (like admin-users.html pattern) - Global search bar - Pagination (configurable page size: 25/50/100/200) - **Export button** — CSV download of current filtered/full dataset - Date range filter (since all tables have timestamps) - Dark/light theme support (reuse existing CSS variables) ### 3. Backend: New API endpoints **File:** `cmd/unified-server/main.go` (or new file `cmd/unified-server/admin_mcp.go`) ``` GET /api/admin/mcp/chat-questions?limit=50&offset=0&sort=timestamp&order=desc&search=... GET /api/admin/mcp/tool-usage?limit=50&offset=0&sort=timestamp&order=desc GET /api/admin/mcp/ai-queries?limit=50&offset=0&sort=timestamp&order=desc GET /api/admin/mcp/export?table=chat_questions&format=csv ``` All endpoints: - Protected by `checkAdminAccess()` (session admin or password) - Query DuckDB via the existing `duckDB` global connection - Return JSON with `{data: [...], total: N, limit: N, offset: N}` - Export endpoint streams CSV with `Content-Disposition: attachment` ### 4. Route registration **File:** `cmd/unified-server/main.go` (in the admin routes section ~line 8845) ```go http.HandleFunc("/admin/mcp", authManager.OptionalAuth(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { // Serve admin-mcp.html from embedded content })) ``` ### 5. Files to modify | File | Change | |------|--------| | `cmd/unified-server/public_html/admin-users.html` | Add tab bar navigation at top | | `cmd/unified-server/main.go` | Add tab bar to uploads/tracks handlers, add `/admin/mcp` route, register API endpoints | | **New:** `cmd/unified-server/public_html/admin-mcp.html` | Full MCP analytics page | | **New:** `cmd/unified-server/admin_mcp.go` | API handlers for MCP data queries + CSV export | ### 6. Tab bar design ```html
Users Uploads Tracks MCP Analytics Realtime
``` The tab bar will pass the admin password via query param in the href (same pattern as existing cross-page links in uploads/tracks). ## Verification 1. Build: `/usr/local/go/bin/go build -o safecast-new-map ./cmd/unified-server/` 2. Run locally with `bash local-server-config.sh` 3. Visit `/admin/users`, `/admin/uploads`, `/admin/tracks` — verify tab bar appears on all 4. Visit `/admin/mcp` — verify all 3 sub-tabs show data from DuckLake tables 5. Test CSV export downloads 6. Test search/filter/sort/pagination 7. Test dark mode

1→// DuckDB Analytics Initialization for Unified Server
     2→// Uses DuckLake with PostgreSQL catalog for shared analytics across all services
     3→
     4→package main
     5→
     6→import (
     7→	"database/sql"
     8→	"fmt"
     9→	"log"
    10→	"os"
    11→	"strings"
    12→
    13→	_ "github.com/duckdb/duckdb-go/v2"
    14→)
    15→
    16→var duckDB *sql.DB
    17→
    18→// initDuckDBAnalytics initializes DuckDB with DuckLake catalog backed by PostgreSQL.
    19→// This allows multiple services to share the same analytics tables concurrently.
    20→func initDuckDBAnalytics() error {
    21→	// Open in-memory DuckDB — all persistent data lives in DuckLake (PostgreSQL + Parquet)
    22→	var err error
    23→	duckDB, err = sql.Open("duckdb", "")
    24→	if err != nil {
    25→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open duckdb: %w", err)
    26→	}
    27→
    28→	duckDB.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
    29→	duckDB.SetMaxIdleConns(1)
    30→	duckDB.SetConnMaxLifetime(0)
    31→
    32→	if err := duckDB.Ping(); err != nil {
    33→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to ping duckdb: %w", err)
    34→	}
    35→
    36→	log.Println("DuckDB initialized (in-memory)")
    37→
    38→	// Install and load required extensions
    39→	for _, ext := range []string{"ducklake", "postgres"} {
    40→		if _, err := duckDB.Exec(fmt.Sprintf("INSTALL %s;", ext)); err != nil {
    41→			log.Printf("Warning: INSTALL %s failed: %v", ext, err)
    42→		}
    43→		if _, err := duckDB.Exec(fmt.Sprintf("LOAD %s;", ext)); err != nil {
    44→			return fmt.Errorf("LOAD %s: %w", ext, err)
    45→		}
    46→	}
    47→
    48→	// Attach DuckLake catalog via PostgreSQL
    49→	ducklakePGURL := os.Getenv("DUCKLAKE_PG_URL")
    50→	if ducklakePGURL == "" {
    51→		ducklakePGURL = "dbname=ducklake_catalog host=localhost user=ducklake_rw"
    52→	}
    53→	dataPath := os.Getenv("DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH")
    54→	if dataPath == "" {
    55→		dataPath = "/var/lib/safecast/ducklake/"
    56→	}
    57→
    58→	attachQuery := fmt.Sprintf(
    59→		"ATTACH 'ducklake:postgres:%s' AS analytics (DATA_PATH '%s');",
    60→		ducklakePGURL, dataPath,
    61→	)
    62→	if _, err := duckDB.Exec(attachQuery); err != nil {
    63→		return fmt.Errorf("attach DuckLake: %w", err)
    64→	}
    65→	log.Printf("DuckLake attached (catalog=PostgreSQL, data=%s)", dataPath)
    66→
    67→	// Use analytics as default database
    68→	if _, err := duckDB.Exec("USE analytics;"); err != nil {
    69→		return fmt.Errorf("USE analytics: %w", err)
    70→	}
    71→
    72→	// Also attach main Safecast PostgreSQL for cross-database queries (read-only)
    73→	databaseURL := os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL")
    74→	if databaseURL == "" {
    75→		// Unified server uses -db-conn flag; construct URL from that
    76→		// Fall back to environment variable
    77→	}
    78→	if databaseURL != "" {
    79→		if err := attachPostgres(databaseURL); err != nil {
    80→			log.Printf("Warning: PostgreSQL attach failed: %v (cross-db analytics disabled)", err)
    81→		} else {
    82→			log.Println("Safecast PostgreSQL attached for cross-database queries")
    83→		}
    84→	}
    85→
    86→	// Create analytics schema in DuckLake
    87→	if err := createDuckDBSchema(); err != nil {
    88→		log.Printf("Warning: failed to create DuckLake schema: %v", err)
    89→	}
    90→
    91→	return nil
    92→}
    93→
    94→// attachPostgres attaches the main Safecast PostgreSQL for read-only cross-database queries
    95→func attachPostgres(databaseURL string) error {
    96→	attachStr := databaseURL
    97→	if !strings.Contains(databaseURL, "?") {
    98→		attachStr = databaseURL + "?sslmode=prefer"
    99→	}
   100→
   101→	query := fmt.Sprintf("ATTACH '%s' AS postgres_db (TYPE POSTGRES, READ_ONLY);", attachStr)
   102→	if _, err := duckDB.Exec(query); err != nil {
   103→		return fmt.Errorf("attach postgres: %w", err)
   104→	}
   105→	return nil
   106→}
   107→
   108→// createDuckDBSchema creates the shared analytics tables in DuckLake
   109→func createDuckDBSchema() error {
   110→	// DuckLake doesn't support multi-statement exec, so run each separately
   111→	tables := []string{
   112→		`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mcp_query_log (
   113→			tool_name VARCHAR,
   114→			timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
   115→			duration_ms BIGINT,
   116→			result_count INTEGER,
   117→			client VARCHAR,
   118→			user_id VARCHAR,
   119→			user_email VARCHAR
   120→		)`,
   121→		`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mcp_ai_query_log (
   122→			user_id VARCHAR,
   123→			user_email VARCHAR,
   124→			session_id VARCHAR,
   125→			timestamp TIMESTAMP,
   126→			tool_name VARCHAR,
   127→			generated_query VARCHAR,
   128→			duration_ms BIGINT,
   129→			commit_hash VARCHAR,
   130→			error VARCHAR
   131→		)`,
   132→		`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chat_questions (
   133→			id BIGINT,
   134→			timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
   135→			question VARCHAR,
   136→			source VARCHAR,
   137→			ip_address VARCHAR,
   138→			user_agent VARCHAR,
   139→			is_mobile BOOLEAN,
   140→			os VARCHAR,
   141→			browser VARCHAR,
   142→			country VARCHAR,
   143→			accept_language VARCHAR,
   144→			referer VARCHAR,
   145→			session_id VARCHAR,
   146→			history_length INTEGER,
   147→			model VARCHAR,
   148→			cloudfront BOOLEAN,
   149→			client_timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ,
   150→			answer VARCHAR
   151→		)`,
   152→	}
   153→
   154→	for _, ddl := range tables {
   155→		if _, err := duckDB.Exec(ddl); err != nil {
   156→			return fmt.Errorf("create schema: %w", err)
   157→		}
   158→	}
   159→
   160→	log.Println("DuckLake analytics schema ready")
   161→	return nil
   162→}
   163→
   164→// duckDBAvailable returns true if DuckDB is initialized
   165→func duckDBAvailable() bool {
   166→	return duckDB != nil
   167→}

   164→func GetToolUsageStats() ([]map[string]any, error) {
   165→	if duckDB == nil {

   185→		if err := rows.Scan(&toolName, &calls, &avgDur, &maxDur); err != nil {

   198→// QueryPostgresAnalytics executes an analytical query on the attached Postgres DB.
   199→func QueryPostgresAnalytics(query string, args ...any) ([]map[string]any, error) {
   200→	if duckDB == nil {
   201→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("duckdb not initialized")
   202→	}
   203→
   204→	rows, err := duckDB.Query(query, args...)
   205→	if err != nil {
   206→		return nil, err
   207→	}
   208→	defer rows.Close()
   209→
   210→	cols, err := rows.Columns()
   211→	if err != nil {
   212→		return nil, err
   213→	}
   214→
   215→	var results []map[string]any
   216→	for rows.Next() {
   217→		columns := make([]interface{}, len(cols))
   218→		columnPointers := make([]interface{}, len(cols))
   219→		for i := range columns {
   220→			columnPointers[i] = &columns[i]
   221→		}
   222→
   223→		if err := rows.Scan(columnPointers...); err != nil {
   224→			return nil, err
   225→		}
   226→
   227→		row := make(map[string]any)
   228→		for i, colName := range cols {
   229→			val := columns[i]
   230→			if b, ok := val.([]byte); ok {
   231→				row[colName] = string(b)
   232→			} else {
   233→				row[colName] = val
   234→			}
   235→		}
   236→		results = append(results, row)
   237→	}
   238→	return results, nil
   239→}

    16→var duckDB *sql.DB
    17→
    18→// initDuckDBAnalytics initializes DuckDB with DuckLake catalog backed by PostgreSQL.
    19→// This allows multiple services to share the same analytics tables concurrently.
    20→func initDuckDBAnalytics() error {
    21→	// Open in-memory DuckDB — all persistent data lives in DuckLake (PostgreSQL + Parquet)
    22→	var err error
    23→	duckDB, err = sql.Open("duckdb", "")
    24→	if err != nil {
    25→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open duckdb: %w", err)
    26→	}
    27→
    28→	duckDB.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
    29→	duckDB.SetMaxIdleConns(1)
    30→	duckDB.SetConnMaxLifetime(0)
    31→
    32→	if err := duckDB.Ping(); err != nil {
    33→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to ping duckdb: %w", err)
    34→	}
    35→
    36→	log.Println("DuckDB initialized (in-memory)")
    37→
    38→	// Install and load required extensions
    39→	for _, ext := range []string{"ducklake", "postgres"} {
    40→		if _, err := duckDB.Exec(fmt.Sprintf("INSTALL %s;", ext)); err != nil {
    41→			log.Printf("Warning: INSTALL %s failed: %v", ext, err)
    42→		}
    43→		if _, err := duckDB.Exec(fmt.Sprintf("LOAD %s;", ext)); err != nil {
    44→			return fmt.Errorf("LOAD %s: %w", ext, err)
    45→		}
    46→	}
    47→
    48→	// Attach DuckLake catalog via PostgreSQL
    49→	ducklakePGURL := os.Getenv("DUCKLAKE_PG_URL")
    50→	if ducklakePGURL == "" {
    51→		ducklakePGURL = "dbname=ducklake_catalog host=localhost user=ducklake_rw"
    52→	}
    53→	dataPath := os.Getenv("DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH")
    54→	if dataPath == "" {
    55→		dataPath = "/var/lib/safecast/ducklake/"
    56→	}
    57→
    58→	attachQuery := fmt.Sprintf(
    59→		"ATTACH 'ducklake:postgres:%s' AS analytics (DATA_PATH '%s');",
    60→		ducklakePGURL, dataPath,
    61→	)
    62→	if _, err := duckDB.Exec(attachQuery); err != nil {
    63→		return fmt.Errorf("attach DuckLake: %w", err)
    64→	}
    65→	log.Printf("DuckLake attached (catalog=PostgreSQL, data=%s)", dataPath)
    66→
    67→	// Use analytics as default database
    68→	if _, err := duckDB.Exec("USE analytics;"); err != nil {
    69→		return fmt.Errorf("USE analytics: %w", err)
    70→	}
    71→
    72→	// Also attach main Safecast PostgreSQL for cross-database queries (read-only)
    73→	databaseURL := os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL")
    74→	if databaseURL == "" {
    75→		// Unified server uses -db-conn flag; construct URL from that
    76→		// Fall back to environment variable
    77→	}
    78→	if databaseURL != "" {
    79→		if err := attachPostgres(databaseURL); err != nil {
    80→			log.Printf("Warning: PostgreSQL attach failed: %v (cross-db analytics disabled)", err)
    81→		} else {
    82→			log.Println("Safecast PostgreSQL attached for cross-database queries")
    83→		}
    84→	}
    85→
    86→	// Create analytics schema in DuckLake
    87→	if err := createDuckDBSchema(); err != nil {
    88→		log.Printf("Warning: failed to create DuckLake schema: %v", err)
    89→	}
    90→
    91→	return nil
    92→}
    93→
    94→// attachPostgres attaches the main Safecast PostgreSQL for read-only cross-database queries
    95→func attachPostgres(databaseURL string) error {
    96→	attachStr := databaseURL
    97→	if !strings.Contains(databaseURL, "?") {
    98→		attachStr = databaseURL + "?sslmode=prefer"
    99→	}
   100→
   101→	query := fmt.Sprintf("ATTACH '%s' AS postgres_db (TYPE POSTGRES, READ_ONLY);", attachStr)
   102→	if _, err := duckDB.Exec(query); err != nil {
   103→		return fmt.Errorf("attach postgres: %w", err)
   104→	}
   105→	return nil
   106→}

   110→	// DuckLake doesn't support multi-statement exec, so run each separately
   111→	tables := []string{
   112→		`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mcp_query_log (
   113→			tool_name VARCHAR,
   114→			timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
   115→			duration_ms BIGINT,
   116→			result_count INTEGER,
   117→			client VARCHAR,
   118→			user_id VARCHAR,

   136→			source VARCHAR,
   137→			ip_address VARCHAR,

   171→// sanitizeQuery normalizes whitespace and scrubs obvious literal values.
   172→// This helps avoid logging sensitive data while retaining query structure.
   173→func sanitizeQuery(q string) string {
   174→	if q == "" {
   175→		return ""
   176→	}
   177→
   178→	// Collapse all whitespace (including newlines) to single spaces.
   179→	q = strings.Join(strings.Fields(q), " ")
   180→
   181→	// Replace string literals with a placeholder.
   182→	q = singleQuotedLiteral.ReplaceAllString(q, "'?'")
   183→
   184→	// Truncate overly long queries to avoid oversized log lines.
   185→	const maxLen = 1000
   186→	if len(q) > maxLen {

   201→// newSessionID generates a RFC4122-ish random UUID v4 string.
   202→func newSessionID() string {
   203→	var b [16]byte
   204→	if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
   205→		// In the unlikely event of failure, return empty string rather than blocking.
   206→		return ""
   207→	}
   208→
   209→	// Set version (4) and variant bits.
   210→	b[6] = (b[6] & 0x0f) | 0x40
   211→	b[8] = (b[8] & 0x3f) | 0x80
   212→
   213→	return formatUUID(b)
   214→}
   215→
   216→func formatUUID(b [16]byte) string {
   217→	return strings.ToLower(
   218→		strings.Join([]string{
   219→			sprintf8(b[0:4]),
   220→			sprintf4(b[4:6]),
   221→			sprintf4(b[6:8]),
   222→			sprintf4(b[8:10]),
   223→			sprintf8(b[10:14]) + sprintf2(b[14:16]),
   224→		}, "-"),
   225→	)
   226→}
   227→
   228→func sprintf2(b []byte) string {
   229→	return sprintfN(b, 2)
   230→}
   231→
   232→func sprintf4(b []byte) string {
   233→	return sprintfN(b, 4)
   234→}
   235→
   236→func sprintf8(b []byte) string {
   237→	return sprintfN(b, 4) // 4 bytes → 8 hex chars
   238→}
   239→
   240→func sprintfN(b []byte, byteCount int) string {
   241→	if len(b) < byteCount {
   242→		byteCount = len(b)
   243→	}
   244→	val := uint64(0)
   245→	for i := 0; i < byteCount; i++ {
   246→		val = (val << 8) | uint64(b[i])
   247→	}
   248→	width := byteCount * 2
   249→	buf := make([]byte, width)
   250→	for i := width - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
   251→		buf[i] = "0123456789abcdef"[val&0xf]
   252→		val >>= 4
   253→	}
   254→	return string(buf)
   255→}

    16→func logChatQuestion(r *http.Request, question, source, model, sessionID string, historyLen int, clientTimestamp string) int64 {

    25→	ip := getClientIP(r)

    27→	isMobile, osName, browser := parseUserAgent(ua)

    29→	acceptLang := r.Header.Get("Accept-Language")
    30→	if len(acceptLang) > 200 {

    37→
    38→	// Parse client timestamp; use nil if not provided or invalid

    40→	if clientTimestamp != "" {
    41→		clientTS = clientTimestamp
    42→	}

    44→	// Generate unique ID (DuckLake doesn't support RETURNING or sequences)
    45→	id := time.Now().UnixNano()

    51→			session_id, history_length, model, cloudfront, client_timestamp

    80→// getClientIP extracts the client IP from the request, respecting proxy headers.
    81→func getClientIP(r *http.Request) string {
    82→	// X-Forwarded-For may contain multiple IPs: client, proxy1, proxy2
    83→	if xff := r.Header.Get("X-Forwarded-For"); xff != "" {
    84→		parts := strings.SplitN(xff, ",", 2)
    85→		ip := strings.TrimSpace(parts[0])
    86→		if ip != "" {
    87→			return ip
    88→		}
    89→	}
    90→	if xri := r.Header.Get("X-Real-IP"); xri != "" {
    91→		return strings.TrimSpace(xri)
    92→	}
    93→	host, _, err := net.SplitHostPort(r.RemoteAddr)
    94→	if err != nil {
    95→		return r.RemoteAddr
    96→	}
    97→	return host
    98→}

   100→// parseUserAgent extracts mobile/desktop, OS, and browser from User-Agent string.
   101→func parseUserAgent(ua string) (isMobile bool, osName, browser string) {
   102→	lower := strings.ToLower(ua)
   103→
   104→	// Mobile detection
   105→	isMobile = strings.Contains(lower, "mobile") ||
   106→		strings.Contains(lower, "android") && !strings.Contains(lower, "tablet") ||
   107→		strings.Contains(lower, "iphone") ||
   108→		strings.Contains(lower, "ipod")
   109→
   110→	// OS detection
   111→	switch {
   112→	case strings.Contains(lower, "iphone") || strings.Contains(lower, "ipad") || strings.Contains(lower, "ipod"):
   113→		osName = "iOS"
   114→	case strings.Contains(lower, "android"):
   115→		osName = "Android"
   116→	case strings.Contains(lower, "windows"):
   117→		osName = "Windows"
   118→	case strings.Contains(lower, "macintosh") || strings.Contains(lower, "mac os"):
   119→		osName = "macOS"
   120→	case strings.Contains(lower, "linux"):
   121→		osName = "Linux"
   122→	case strings.Contains(lower, "cros"):
   123→		osName = "ChromeOS"
   124→	default:
   125→		osName = "Unknown"
   126→	}
   127→
   128→	// Browser detection (order matters — check specific before generic)
   129→	switch {
   130→	case strings.Contains(lower, "edg/") || strings.Contains(lower, "edge/"):
   131→		browser = "Edge"
   132→	case strings.Contains(lower, "opr/") || strings.Contains(lower, "opera"):
   133→		browser = "Opera"
   134→	case strings.Contains(lower, "firefox/"):
   135→		browser = "Firefox"
   136→	case strings.Contains(lower, "chrome/") && !strings.Contains(lower, "chromium"):
   137→		browser = "Chrome"
   138→	case strings.Contains(lower, "safari/") && !strings.Contains(lower, "chrome"):
   139→		browser = "Safari"
   140→	case strings.Contains(lower, "chromium"):
   141→		browser = "Chromium"
   142→	default:
   143→		browser = "Unknown"
   144→	}
   145→
   146→	return
   147→}

    87→				MAX(doserate) AS max_value

    99→				AVG(doserate) AS avg_value

   146→## CloudFront Considerations
   147→
   148→### Cache Invalidation
   149→
   150→After deploying new code, CloudFront may serve cached versions of static files. Create an invalidation to force cache refresh:
   151→
   152→```bash
   153→# Invalidate all cached content
   154→aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id E12FYIQ8RRXOJ1 --paths "/*"
   155→
   156→# Invalidate specific paths
   157→aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id E12FYIQ8RRXOJ1 --paths "/index.html" "/static/*"
   158→```
   159→
   160→**Cost:** First 1,000 invalidation paths per month are free, then $0.005 per path.
   161→
   162→### Cache Behavior
   163→
   164→Current configuration:
   165→- **API endpoints:** No caching (Cache-Control headers prevent it)
   166→- **Static files:** Cached at edge locations
   167→- **Uploads:** Not cached (Cache-Control: private)
   168→- **Admin pages:** Not cached (Cache-Control: no-store)
   169→
   170→### WAF Configuration
   171→
   172→AWS WAF protects against:
   173→- SQL injection
   174→- Cross-site scripting (XSS)
   175→- ~~Large request bodies~~ (Changed to "Count" mode for file uploads)
   176→
   177→**Important:** `SizeRestrictions_BODY` rule is in "Count" mode to allow large file uploads. See [docs/cloudfront-fix-waf-403.md](cloudfront-fix-waf-403.md) for details.
   178→
   179→## Analytics (DuckLake)
   180→
   181→Both the unified server and MCP server use DuckLake for analytics (tool usage logs, chat questions). Architecture: in-memory DuckDB attaches a shared DuckLake catalog backed by PostgreSQL + Parquet files, allowing concurrent access from multiple services.

   183→**Required env vars** (set in `.env` files or systemd service):
   184→- `DUCKLAKE_PG_URL` — PostgreSQL connection for DuckLake catalog (e.g., `dbname=ducklake_catalog host=localhost user=ducklake_rw`)
   185→- `DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH` — Directory for Parquet data files (e.g., `/var/lib/safecast/ducklake/`)
   186→
   187→**Shared tables:** `chat_questions`, `mcp_query_log`, `mcp_ai_query_log`

- `DUCKLAKE_PG_URL` — PostgreSQL connection for DuckLake catalog (e.g., `dbname=ducklake_catalog host=localhost user=ducklake_rw`)

```bash

        /* Manual theme overrides */

        .theme-icon {

        .theme-switch {
          position: relative;
          display: inline-block;
          width: 30px;
          height: 16px;
          margin: 0 4px;
        }

        .theme-switch input {
          opacity: 0;
          width: 0;
          height: 0;
        }

        .theme-slider {
          position: absolute;
          cursor: pointer;
          top: 0;
          left: 0;
          right: 0;
          bottom: 0;
          background-color: #ccc;
          transition: 0.2s;
          border-radius: 16px;
        }

        .theme-slider:before {
          position: absolute;
          content: "";
          height: 12px;
          width: 12px;
          left: 2px;
          bottom: 2px;
          background-color: #fff;
          transition: 0.2s;
          border-radius: 50%;
        }

        .theme-switch input:checked + .theme-slider {
          background-color: var(--link-color);
        }

        .theme-switch input:checked + .theme-slider:before {
          transform: translateX(14px);
        }

        #map {

          box-shadow: 0px 0px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.3);
        }

        /* Consistent hover/focus hints for interactive controls */
        .control-tooltip {
          position: fixed;
          z-index: 1400;
          pointer-events: none;
          background: var(--modal-bg);
          color: var(--modal-text);
          border: var(--legend-border);
          border-radius: 8px;

          box-shadow: 0 6px 18px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35);

          opacity: 0;
          transform: scale(0.96);
          transform-origin: center;
          transition: opacity 120ms ease, transform 120ms ease;
          text-align: left;
        }

        .control-tooltip--visible {
          opacity: 1;

        .control-tooltip__title {

        .control-tooltip__list {

        .upload-btn {

        /* File upload overlay */
        #fileOverlay {
          position: fixed;
          top: 0;
          left: 0;

          justify-content: center;
          align-items: center;

        /* Upload progress container */
        #fileProgressContainer {
          background-color: var(--progress-bg);
          color: var(--progress-color);

          border-radius: 10px;

          width: 100%;

          margin-bottom: 15px;

          margin-bottom: 5px;

        /* Progress bar */
        .progress-bar {
          width: 100%;
          height: 10px;
          background-color: var(--progress-bar-bg);
          border-radius: 5px;
          overflow: hidden;
        }

        .progress-bar-inner {
          height: 100%;
          background-opacity: 1;
          width: 0%;

        /* Progress bar striped animation for server processing */
        .progress-bar-inner.processing {
          background-image: linear-gradient(
            45deg,
            rgba(255,255,255,.15) 25%,
            transparent 25%,
            transparent 50%,
            rgba(255,255,255,.15) 50%,
            rgba(255,255,255,.15) 75%,
            transparent 75%,
            transparent

          background-size: 40px 40px;
          animation: progress-stripes 1s linear infinite;

        @keyframes progress-stripes {
          0% {
            background-position: 0 0;

          100% {

        /* ─────────–– Slider clean-look patch ─────────── */

        #dateSlider .noUi-base{
          background:#bfbfbf;
          width:100%;                /* 6px width */
          height:100%;               /* 130px minus padding */
        }

        /* Slider handles respect theme colors */
        .noUi-vertical .noUi-handle{
          width:32px;
          height:20px;

          background: var(--control-bg);      /* follow theme */

          box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.25);

          /* copied parameters from #dateSlider */

          margin:16px auto 26px;     /* same margins */

          animation:spin 1s linear infinite;

        .qr-btn {
          background: var(--control-bg);
          border: var(--legend-border);
          border-radius: var(--btn-border-radius);
          width: 44px; height: 44px;
          padding: 8px;

				/* ---- Unified tooltip/popup sizing & wrapping ----
					 Keep tooltip (hover) and popup (click) the same width.
					 Leaflet's default popup maxWidth is ~300px, so we reuse that.

				:root {
					--tooltip-max: 300px;   /* single source of truth for both tooltip & popup widths */
					--tooltip-min: 220px;   /* prevents collapsing into a thin vertical strip */
				}

				.live-tooltip {

				.leaflet-tooltip.custom-tooltip {
					white-space: normal;            /* allow line wrapping */
					max-width: var(--tooltip-max);  /* match popup max width */
					min-inline-size: var(--tooltip-min); /* avoid skinny column */
					overflow-wrap: break-word;      /* break long words/URLs only when needed */
					word-break: break-word;         /* compatibility for older browsers */
					hyphens: auto;                  /* nicer hyphenation when available */
				}

				/* Leaflet popup content (click). Enforce the same max width to match tooltip. */
				.leaflet-popup-content {

    <!-- Translation script -->
    <script id="translations-script">
      // Translation object passed from Go
      // We emit ready-made JS literals to keep html/template from misdetecting
      // the surrounding string context when translations contain quotes.
      var translations = {{ .TranslationsJSON }};
        var currentLang = '{{ .Lang }}'; // Current language

        // Get translation by key
        function translate(key) {
            if (!translations['en']) {
                console.error('English translations not available!');
                return key;
            }

            if (translations[currentLang] && translations[currentLang][key]) {
                return translations[currentLang][key];
            } else if (translations['en'][key]) {
                return translations['en'][key];
            }
            return key;
        }
    </script>

// parseColor extracts RGB components from either hex (#rrggbb) or rgb(r,g,b)
// strings.  Keeping this helper local avoids pulling external libraries while
// letting us reuse the logic for alpha blending and contrast checks.
function parseColor(color) {
  if (!color) return null;
  if (color.startsWith('#')) {
    const hex = color.slice(1);
    if (hex.length === 6) {
      return {
        r: parseInt(hex.slice(0, 2), 16),
        g: parseInt(hex.slice(2, 4), 16),
        b: parseInt(hex.slice(4, 6), 16),
      };
    }
    if (hex.length === 3) {
      return {
        r: parseInt(hex[0] + hex[0], 16),
        g: parseInt(hex[1] + hex[1], 16),
        b: parseInt(hex[2] + hex[2], 16),
      };
    }
  }
  if (color.startsWith('rgb')) {
    const parts = color.match(/\d+/g);
    if (parts && parts.length >= 3) {
      return {
        r: parseInt(parts[0], 10),
        g: parseInt(parts[1], 10),
        b: parseInt(parts[2], 10),

  }
  return null;
}

function colorWithAlpha(color, alpha) {

  if (!rgb) return color;
  const a = Math.min(Math.max(alpha, 0), 1);
  return `rgba(${rgb.r}, ${rgb.g}, ${rgb.b}, ${a})`;
}

function isDarkColor(color) {

  const luminance = 0.299 * rgb.r + 0.587 * rgb.g + 0.114 * rgb.b;

  insertIntoChildren(point) {
    if (this.nw.contains(point)) this.nw.insert(point);
    else if (this.ne.contains(point)) this.ne.insert(point);
    else if (this.sw.contains(point)) this.sw.insert(point);
    else if (this.se.contains(point)) this.se.insert(point);
  }

  insert(point) {
    if (!this.contains(point)) return false;

    if (!this.divided) {
      if (this.points.length < this.capacity || this.depth >= this.maxDepth) {
        this.points.push(point);
        return true;
      }
      this.subdivide();
    }

    this.insertIntoChildren(point);
    return true;
  }

  remove(point) {
    if (!this.contains(point)) return false;

    if (!this.divided) {
      const idx = this.points.findIndex(p => p.id === point.id);
      if (idx !== -1) {
        this.points.splice(idx, 1);
        return true;
      }
      return false;
    }

    return this.nw.remove(point) || this.ne.remove(point) ||
           this.sw.remove(point) || this.se.remove(point);
  }

  // Query all points within a bounding box
  queryRange(range, found = []) {
    if (!this.intersects(range)) return found;

    if (!this.divided) {
      for (const p of this.points) {
        if (p.lat >= range.minLat && p.lat <= range.maxLat &&
            p.lon >= range.minLon && p.lon <= range.maxLon) {
          found.push(p);
        }
      }
    } else {
      this.nw.queryRange(range, found);
      this.ne.queryRange(range, found);
      this.sw.queryRange(range, found);
      this.se.queryRange(range, found);
    }

    return found;
  }

  // Query all points NOT within a bounding box (for viewport culling)
  queryOutside(range, found = []) {
    // If this node doesn't intersect the range, all points are outside
    if (!this.intersects(range)) {
      this.getAllPoints(found);
      return found;
    }

    if (!this.divided) {
      for (const p of this.points) {
        if (p.lat < range.minLat || p.lat > range.maxLat ||
            p.lon < range.minLon || p.lon > range.maxLon) {
          found.push(p);
        }
      }
    } else {
      this.nw.queryOutside(range, found);
      this.ne.queryOutside(range, found);
      this.sw.queryOutside(range, found);
      this.se.queryOutside(range, found);
    }

    return found;
  }

  getAllPoints(found = []) {
    if (!this.divided) {
      found.push(...this.points);
    } else {
      this.nw.getAllPoints(found);
      this.ne.getAllPoints(found);
      this.sw.getAllPoints(found);
      this.se.getAllPoints(found);
    }
    return found;
  }

  // Find nearest point with optional filter function
  findNearest(lat, lon, filter = null) {
    let nearest = null;
    let minDistSq = Infinity;

    const search = (node) => {
      if (!node) return;

      // Quick check: could this node contain a closer point?
      const nodeDist = this.pointToRectDistSq(lat, lon, node.bounds);
      if (nodeDist >= minDistSq) return;

      if (!node.divided) {
        for (const p of node.points) {
          if (filter && !filter(p)) continue;
          const distSq = (p.lat - lat) ** 2 + (p.lon - lon) ** 2;
          if (distSq < minDistSq) {
            minDistSq = distSq;
            nearest = p;
          }
        }
      } else {
        // Search children in order of distance
        const children = [node.nw, node.ne, node.sw, node.se]
          .map(c => ({ node: c, dist: this.pointToRectDistSq(lat, lon, c.bounds) }))
          .sort((a, b) => a.dist - b.dist);

        for (const { node: child } of children) {
          search(child);
        }
      }
    };

    search(this);
    return nearest;
  }

  pointToRectDistSq(lat, lon, rect) {
    const dx = Math.max(rect.minLon - lon, 0, lon - rect.maxLon);
    const dy = Math.max(rect.minLat - lat, 0, lat - rect.maxLat);
    return dx * dx + dy * dy;
  }

  clear() {
    this.points = [];
    this.divided = false;
    this.nw = this.ne = this.sw = this.se = null;
  }

  get size() {
    if (!this.divided) return this.points.length;
    return this.nw.size + this.ne.size + this.sw.size + this.se.size;
  }
}

/**
 * Load previously saved speed-filter state from sessionStorage.
 * If nothing is stored yet, return defaults that reflect backend capabilities.
 *   Realtime on:  Safecast heart on, ✈️ off, 🚗 on, 🚶 on  (as requested).
 *   Realtime off: ✈️ off, 🚗 on, 🚶 on  (heart absent).
 */
function loadSpeedFilterState() {
  // We derive defaults from the realtime flag so the UI matches backend capabilities.
  const base = { plane: false, car: true, ped: true, spectrum: true };
  if (window.safecastRealtimeEnabled) {
    base.live = true;
  }
  try {
    const raw = sessionStorage.getItem('speedFilterState');
    const st = raw ? JSON.parse(raw) : {};
    const merged = Object.assign({}, base, st);
    if (!window.safecastRealtimeEnabled) {
      delete merged.live;
    }
    // Ensure spectrum key exists for older saved states
    if (merged.spectrum === undefined) merged.spectrum = true;
    return merged;
  } catch (e) {
    return base;
  }
}

 * Safari shows "Aug 2025", etc.

function tsToNiceStr(ts){
  return new Date(ts * 1000)
    .toLocaleDateString(undefined, { month: 'short', year: 'numeric' });
}


// absolute month difference between two unix timestamps
function monthsApart(ts0, ts1){
  const d0 = new Date(ts0 * 1000);
  const d1 = new Date(ts1 * 1000);
  return Math.abs((d1.getFullYear() - d0.getFullYear()) * 12 +
    (d1.getMonth()     - d0.getMonth()));
}

  // Set height
  legendBox.style.height = (typeof currentColoring !== 'undefined' && currentColoring === 'chicha') ? '180px' : '500px';

  // Build gradient string manually for maximum compatibility
  var colorStrings = [];
  for (var i = 0; i < steps.length; i++) {
    colorStrings.push('rgb(' + steps[i].color.join(',') + ')');
  }
  
  // Apply gradient
  var gradientStyle = 'linear-gradient(to top, ' + colorStrings.join(', ') + ')';
  bar.style.backgroundImage = gradientStyle;
  bar.style.backgroundColor = '#333';
  bar.style.height = '100%';

  // Update labels
  labelsContainer.innerHTML = '';
  // Clone and reverse without spread for compatibility
  var stepsToRender = steps.slice().reverse();
  for (var j = 0; j < stepsToRender.length; j++) {
    var step = stepsToRender[j];
    var el = document.createElement('span');
    var val = step.uSv;
    if (!isUSv) {
       val = val * 100;
       if (val >= 100) val = Math.round(val);
       else if (val >= 10) val = parseFloat(val.toFixed(1));
       else val = parseFloat(val.toFixed(2));
    }
    el.textContent = val;
    labelsContainer.appendChild(el);
  }
}

/**
 * Attach a lightweight tooltip to a control so every hint shares one theme-aware renderer.
 * We return show/hide/destroy handlers to let callers reuse a single tooltip while controls collapse.
 */
function attachControlTooltip(target, options) {
  if (!target) {
    return {
      hide: function noopHide() {},
      destroy: function noopDestroy() {},
    };
  }

  const opts = Object.assign({
    placement: 'top',
    html: false,
    maxWidth: 280,
  }, options || {});

  let tooltipEl = null;

  function resolveContent() {
    const content = typeof opts.content === 'function' ? opts.content() : opts.content;
    return content || '';
  }

  function positionTooltip() {
    if (!tooltipEl || !target) {
      return;
    }
    const rect = target.getBoundingClientRect();
    if (rect.width === 0 && rect.height === 0) {
      return;
    }
    const tipRect = tooltipEl.getBoundingClientRect();
    const margin = 10;
    let left = rect.left + (rect.width / 2) - (tipRect.width / 2);
    let top = rect.top - tipRect.height - margin;

    switch (opts.placement) {
      case 'bottom':
        top = rect.bottom + margin;
        left = rect.left + (rect.width / 2) - (tipRect.width / 2);
        break;
      case 'left':
        left = rect.left - tipRect.width - margin;
        top = rect.top + (rect.height / 2) - (tipRect.height / 2);
        break;
      case 'right':
        left = rect.right + margin;
        top = rect.top + (rect.height / 2) - (tipRect.height / 2);
        break;
      default:
        // keep default top placement
        break;
    }

    const viewportPadding = 8;
    left = Math.max(viewportPadding, Math.min(left, window.innerWidth - tipRect.width - viewportPadding));
    top = Math.max(viewportPadding, Math.min(top, window.innerHeight - tipRect.height - viewportPadding));
    tooltipEl.style.left = left + 'px';
    tooltipEl.style.top = top + 'px';
  }

  function showTooltip() {
    if (!target || !target.isConnected) {
      return;
    }
    const rects = target.getClientRects();
    if (!rects || rects.length === 0) {
      return;
    }
    const content = resolveContent();
    if (!content) {
      return;
    }
    if (tooltipEl) {
      if (opts.html) {
        tooltipEl.innerHTML = content;
      } else {
        tooltipEl.textContent = content;
      }
      positionTooltip();
      return;
    }
    tooltipEl = document.createElement('div');
    tooltipEl.className = 'control-tooltip';
    tooltipEl.setAttribute('role', 'tooltip');
    const maxWidth = typeof opts.maxWidth === 'number' ? opts.maxWidth + 'px' : opts.maxWidth;
    tooltipEl.style.maxWidth = maxWidth;
    if (opts.html) {
      tooltipEl.innerHTML = content;
    } else {
      tooltipEl.textContent = content;
    }
    document.body.appendChild(tooltipEl);
    positionTooltip();
    window.addEventListener('scroll', positionTooltip, true);
    window.addEventListener('resize', positionTooltip);
    requestAnimationFrame(function () {
      if (tooltipEl) {
        tooltipEl.classList.add('control-tooltip--visible');
      }
    });
  }

  function hideTooltip() {
    if (!tooltipEl) {
      return;
    }
    window.removeEventListener('scroll', positionTooltip, true);
    window.removeEventListener('resize', positionTooltip);
    const el = tooltipEl;
    tooltipEl = null;
    el.classList.remove('control-tooltip--visible');
    setTimeout(function () {
      if (el.parentNode) {
        el.parentNode.removeChild(el);
      }
    }, 150);
  }

  function destroyTooltip() {
    hideTooltip();
    target.removeEventListener('mouseenter', showTooltip);
    target.removeEventListener('mouseleave', hideTooltip);
    target.removeEventListener('focus', showTooltip);
    target.removeEventListener('blur', hideTooltip);
    target.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);
  }

  function onKeyDown(ev) {
    if (ev.key === 'Escape') {
      hideTooltip();
    }
  }

  target.addEventListener('mouseenter', showTooltip);
  target.addEventListener('mouseleave', hideTooltip);
  target.addEventListener('focus', showTooltip);
  target.addEventListener('blur', hideTooltip);
  target.addEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);

  return {
    show: showTooltip,
    hide: hideTooltip,
    destroy: destroyTooltip,
  };
}

/**
 * Date-range control with two modes:
 *  - YEAR (single handle): labels show full [minYear..maxYear] when NO user filter is active,
 *    otherwise they show the chosen year.
 *  - MONTH (double handle): classic [from..to] range.
 *
 * Key ideas:
 *  • We expose window.__setDateSliderVisibility(show)
 *  • We expose window.__initSliderOnce(minTs,maxTs) for first build
 *  • We expose window.__syncDateSliders(minTs,maxTs) to keep ranges/labels
 *    in sync with the current map viewport on every pan/zoom IF no custom
 *    time filter is set by the user.
 *
 * No globals except 3 window.* hooks; no vendor APIs beyond noUiSlider.
 */
function createDateRangeSlider(){

  if (isTrackView) return;   // no date control in single-track mode

  let sliderBox, yearSlider, monthSlider;
  let mode  = 'year';                // 'year' | 'month'
  let initY = false, initM = false;  // lazy init flags
  let sliderTooltipHandle = null;    // tooltip helper for hover hints

  // We store the "full range" of current viewport to detect
  // whether a saved filter is actually "show all".
  let fullRange = null; // [minTs,maxTs]

  const DateCtrl = L.Control.extend({
    onAdd(){
      sliderBox = L.DomUtil.create('div','leaflet-control-layers date-slider-box');
      sliderBox.style.display = 'none'; // hidden until needed
      sliderBox.innerHTML = `
        <div class="slider-toggle">
          <button id="btnYear"  class="active">Y</button>
          <button id="btnMonth">M</button>
        </div>
        <div id="lblMax" class="slider-label"></div>
        <div id="yearSlider"></div>
        <div id="dateSlider"></div>
        <div id="lblMin" class="slider-label"></div>
        <button id="btnReset" class="slider-reset-btn" title="Reset"> ⟲ </button>
      `;
      sliderBox.setAttribute('role', 'group');
      sliderBox.setAttribute('tabindex', '0');
      sliderBox.setAttribute('aria-label', translate('date_slider_tooltip'));
      sliderTooltipHandle = attachControlTooltip(sliderBox, {
        placement: 'right',
        content: function () { return translate('date_slider_tooltip'); },
        maxWidth: 300,
      });
      return sliderBox;
    }
  });
  new DateCtrl({ position:'topleft' }).addTo(map);

  const btnY = sliderBox.querySelector('#btnYear');
  const btnM = sliderBox.querySelector('#btnMonth');
  const btnReset = sliderBox.querySelector('#btnReset');
  const lblMin = () => sliderBox.querySelector('#lblMin');
  const lblMax = () => sliderBox.querySelector('#lblMax');

  btnY.onclick = () => switchMode('year');
  btnM.onclick = () => switchMode('month');

  // Show/hide the whole control (called from updateMarkers())
  window.__setDateSliderVisibility = (show)=>{
    sliderBox.style.display = show ? 'block' : 'none';
    if(!show) sessionStorage.removeItem('dateRangeState');
    if (!show && sliderTooltipHandle) {
      sliderTooltipHandle.hide();
    }
  };

  // One-time creation of both sliders using initial bounds
  window.__initSliderOnce = (minTs,maxTs)=>{
    if (initY && initM) return;
    fullRange = [minTs,maxTs]; // remember initial "full range"

    // YEAR slider (single handle)
    if(!initY){
      yearSlider = sliderBox.querySelector('#yearSlider');
      const minYear = new Date(minTs*1000).getUTCFullYear();
      const maxYear = new Date(maxTs*1000).getUTCFullYear();

      noUiSlider.create(yearSlider,{
        start      : minYear,                // the handle can sit anywhere; labels decide what to show
        connect    : [true,false],
        orientation: 'vertical',
        direction  : 'rtl',
        step       : 1,
        range      : { min:minYear, max:maxYear },
        format     : wNumb({ decimals:0 })
      });

      // Update labels:
      //  - If NO user filter or filter equals fullRange → show full year bounds.
      //  - Else → show the chosen year.
      yearSlider.noUiSlider.on('update', ([y])=>{
        if (mode !== 'year') return;
        const saved = loadDateRangeState();
        const fr = fullRange || [minTs,maxTs];
        const isFull = !saved || (saved[0] === fr[0] && saved[1] === fr[1]);
        if (isFull){
          const r = yearSlider.noUiSlider.options.range;
          lblMin().textContent = r.min;
          lblMax().textContent = r.max;
        } else {
          lblMin().textContent = y;
          lblMax().textContent = y;
        }
      });
      yearSlider.noUiSlider.on('change', updateDateFilter);
      initY = true;
    }

    // MONTH slider (double handle)
    if(!initM){
      monthSlider = sliderBox.querySelector('#dateSlider');
      noUiSlider.create(monthSlider,{
        start       : [minTs,maxTs],
        connect     : true,
        orientation : 'vertical',
        direction   : 'rtl',
        step        : 3600, // 1 hour
        range       : { min:minTs, max:maxTs },
        format      : wNumb({ decimals:0 })
      });
      monthSlider.noUiSlider.on('update', ()=>{
        if (mode !== 'month') return;
        const [v0, v1] = monthSlider.noUiSlider.get().map(Number);
        lblMin().textContent = tsToNiceStr(v0);
        lblMax().textContent = tsToNiceStr(v1);
      });
      monthSlider.noUiSlider.on('change', updateDateFilter);
      monthSlider.style.display = 'none';
      initM = true;
    }

    // Initial labels = full bounds
    if (mode === 'year'){
      const r = yearSlider.noUiSlider.options.range;
      lblMin().textContent = r.min;
      lblMax().textContent = r.max;
    } else {
      lblMin().textContent = tsToNiceStr(minTs);
      lblMax().textContent = tsToNiceStr(maxTs);
    }
  };

  // Sync ranges and labels to the *current* viewport on every pan/zoom,
  // but ONLY when user has not applied a custom time filter.
  window.__syncDateSliders = (minTs,maxTs)=>{
    if (!initY || !initM) return; // not built yet

    // Detect whether user has a custom time filter (not full range).
    const saved = loadDateRangeState();
    const prevFull = fullRange;
    fullRange = [minTs,maxTs]; // update "full" range to the new viewport

    const hasCustom =
      !!saved && !(saved[0] === prevFull?.[0] && saved[1] === prevFull?.[1]) &&
      !(saved[0] === fullRange[0] && saved[1] === fullRange[1]);

    // Update YEAR slider bounds
    const minYear = new Date(minTs*1000).getUTCFullYear();
    const maxYear = new Date(maxTs*1000).getUTCFullYear();
    yearSlider.noUiSlider.updateOptions({
      range: { min:minYear, max:maxYear }
    }, false);

    // Update MONTH slider bounds
    monthSlider.noUiSlider.updateOptions({
      range: { min:minTs, max:maxTs }
    }, false);

    // If no custom filter → force labels to show full bounds and make month slider span all
    if (!hasCustom){
      if (mode === 'year'){
        const r = yearSlider.noUiSlider.options.range;
        lblMin().textContent = r.min;
        lblMax().textContent = r.max;
      } else {
        monthSlider.noUiSlider.set([minTs,maxTs]);
        lblMin().textContent = tsToNiceStr(minTs);
        lblMax().textContent = tsToNiceStr(maxTs);
      }
      // persist that "no filter" means full range
      saveDateRangeState([minTs,maxTs]);
    }
  };

  // Reset button → drop custom filter and show full bounds of the *current* viewport
  btnReset.onclick = ()=>{
    sessionStorage.removeItem('dateRangeState');
    if (initY && initM){
      const rY = yearSlider.noUiSlider.options.range;
      const rM = monthSlider.noUiSlider.options.range;
      yearSlider.noUiSlider.set(rY.min);      // handle position is cosmetic
      monthSlider.noUiSlider.set([rM.min, rM.max]);

      lblMin().textContent = (mode==='year') ? rY.min : tsToNiceStr(rM.min);
      lblMax().textContent = (mode==='year') ? rY.max : tsToNiceStr(rM.max);

      // remember "no filter" == full range of the viewport
      saveDateRangeState([rM.min, rM.max]);
      debounceUpdateMarkers();
    }
  };

  function switchMode(next){
    if (mode === next) return;

    mode = next;
    btnY.classList.toggle('active', next==='year');
    btnM.classList.toggle('active', next==='month');
    yearSlider.style.display  = next==='year'  ? 'block' : 'none';
    monthSlider.style.display = next==='month' ? 'block' : 'none';

    // Refresh labels on mode switch respecting full/custom state
    const saved = loadDateRangeState();
    const fr = fullRange;
    const isFull = !saved || (fr && saved[0]===fr[0] && saved[1]===fr[1]);

    if (next === 'year'){
      const r = yearSlider.noUiSlider.options.range;
      if (isFull){
        lblMin().textContent = r.min;
        lblMax().textContent = r.max;
      } else {
        const y = +yearSlider.noUiSlider.get();
        lblMin().textContent = y;
        lblMax().textContent = y;
      }
    } else {
      const r = monthSlider.noUiSlider.options.range;
      if (isFull){
        monthSlider.noUiSlider.set([r.min, r.max]);
        lblMin().textContent = tsToNiceStr(r.min);
        lblMax().textContent = tsToNiceStr(r.max);
      } else {
        const [v0, v1] = monthSlider.noUiSlider.get().map(Number);
        lblMin().textContent = tsToNiceStr(v0);
        lblMax().textContent = tsToNiceStr(v1);
      }
    }

    // Do not change filter on mode flip; user intent remains the same
  }

  function updateDateFilter(){
    // YEAR mode → make a full [year..year] month span
    if (mode==='year'){
      const y = +yearSlider.noUiSlider.get();
      const from = Date.UTC(y,0,1)/1000;
      const to   = Date.UTC(y+1,0,1)/1000 - 1;
      saveDateRangeState([from,to]);
    } else {
      saveDateRangeState(monthSlider.noUiSlider.get().map(Number));
    }
    debounceUpdateMarkers();
  }
}

/* ============================================
 * TILE CACHE - Client-side marker data cache
 * ============================================ */
const tileCache = {
  cache: new Map(),
  maxSize: 100, // Cache up to 100 tiles
  ttl: 5 * 60 * 1000, // 5 minutes

  makeKey(zoom, minLat, minLon, maxLat, maxLon) {
    // Round coordinates to reduce cache key variations
    const precision = zoom >= 10 ? 4 : 3;
    return `${zoom}_${minLat.toFixed(precision)}_${minLon.toFixed(precision)}_${maxLat.toFixed(precision)}_${maxLon.toFixed(precision)}`;
  },

  get(key) {
    const entry = this.cache.get(key);
    if (!entry) return null;

    // Check if expired
    if (Date.now() - entry.timestamp > this.ttl) {
      this.cache.delete(key);
      return null;
    }

    entry.lastAccess = Date.now();
    return entry.data;
  },

  set(key, data) {
    // Implement LRU eviction
    if (this.cache.size >= this.maxSize) {
      // Remove oldest accessed entry
      let oldestKey = null;
      let oldestTime = Infinity;
      for (const [k, v] of this.cache.entries()) {
        if (v.lastAccess < oldestTime) {
          oldestTime = v.lastAccess;
          oldestKey = k;
        }
      }
      if (oldestKey) this.cache.delete(oldestKey);
    }

    this.cache.set(key, {
      data: data,
      timestamp: Date.now(),
      lastAccess: Date.now()
    });
  },

  clear() {
    this.cache.clear();
  }
};
